questions.prompt: Who is your favourite cartoon character?
questions.sampleA1: I like Tom. He is funny cat. I watch Tom and Jerry.
questions.sampleA2: My favourite cartoon character is SpongeBob. He is very funny and always happy. I like watching his show because it makes me laugh.
questions.sampleB1: Well, my favourite cartoon character is probably Jerry from Tom and Jerry. I think he is very clever because he always escapes from Tom. Also, the cartoon is really funny and I have watched it since I was a child.
questions.sampleB2: To be honest, my favourite has always been Jerry from Tom and Jerry. There's something I really look up to about how he keeps his cool and always manages to outwit Tom, no matter what. I suppose it's the sheer cleverness that wins me over — plus, the show still cracks me up even now.
questions.uzSampleA1: Menga Tom yoqadi. U kulguli mushuk. Men Tom va Jerryni tomosha qilaman.
questions.uzSampleA2: Mening eng sevimli multfilm qahramonim SpongeBob. U juda kulgili va doim xursand. Uning ko'rsatuvini tomosha qilishni yaxshi ko'raman, chunki u meni kuldiradi.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Xo'sh, mening eng sevimli multfilm qahramonim, ehtimol, Tom va Jerrydan Jerry bo'lsa kerak. Menimcha, u juda aqlli, chunki u doim Tomdan qochib qutuladi.
Bundan tashqari, multfilm juda kulgili va men uni bolaligimdan beri tomosha qilaman.
questions.uzSampleB2: Shubhasiz, mening eng sevimli multfilm qahramonim Buqs Banni. Menga unda eng ko'p yoqadigan narsa uning o'tkir aqli va har qanday vaziyatda raqiblarini dog'da qoldira olish qobiliyati. Bu qahramonning o'ziga xos jozibasi va barcha yoshdagi tomoshabinlarga yoqadigan abadiy maftunkorligi bor. Bundan tashqari, o'sha klassik multfilmlardagi hazil juda murakkab, shuning uchun ham men ularni bugungi kunda ham tomosha qilishdan zavqlanaman.

vocabulary.title: Q1 - Who is your favourite cartoon character?
idioms: never throw in the towel - "hech qachon taslim bo'lmaslik (kurashni davom ettirish)"
a blast from the past - "o'tmishdan esdalik (nostalgia uyg'otuvchi narsa)"
tickle one's funny bone - "kuldirib yubormoq (kulgili qilmoq)"
sentenceStarters: "My all-time favourite cartoon character is... His hilariously futile attempts to..." - "Mening barcha davrlarim uchun sevimli multfilm qahramonim bu… Uning kulgili va befoyda urinishlari…"
"Furthermore, I find his character surprisingly relatable..." - "Bundan tashqari, uning xarakterini hayratlanarli darajada o'zimga yaqin deb topaman…"

questions.sampleAnswer:
My all-time favourite cartoon character is Tom from the legendary show 'Tom and Jerry.' His hilariously futile attempts to catch Jerry never fail to make me laugh, even after all these years. The slapstick humour is timeless.
Furthermore, I find his character surprisingly relatable. Despite constant failure, Tom never gives up, which I think is a great life lesson hidden behind the comedy — the importance of "never throwing in the towel."
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Mening eng sevimli multfilm qahramonim bu "Tom va Jerry" afsonaviy ko'rsatuvidagi Tom. Uning Jerryni tutishga bo'lgan kulgili va behuda urinishlari meni shu yillar davomida hamon kuldirishdan to'xtamaydi. U yerda ishlatilgan qo'pol hazil hech qachon eskirib qolmaydi.

Bundan tashqari, men uning xarakterini hayratlanarli darajada o'zimga yaqin deb bilaman. Doimiy muvaffaqiyatsizlikka qaramay, Tom hech qachon taslim bo'lmaydi, menimcha bu komediyaning ortida yashiringan ajoyib hayot sabog'i — "hech qachon taslim bo'lmaslik"ning muhimligidir.

questions.prompt: Do you prefer sweet food or salty food?
questions.sampleA1: I like sweet food. Chocolate is good. I eat cake.
questions.sampleA2: I prefer salty food. I like chips and pizza. But sometimes I eat ice cream too because it is sweet and cold.
questions.sampleB1: I think I prefer salty food more than sweet food. For example, I really enjoy eating pizza and chips. However, I also like chocolate sometimes. So I would say I mostly prefer salty snacks, but I don't mind a sweet treat once in a while.
questions.sampleB2: Honestly, I'd say I lean towards salty food more often than not. There's just something about crisps or a bag of salted nuts that I find hard to resist. That said, I do have a bit of a sweet tooth now and then, especially after dinner — but if I had to pick sides, savoury would win hands down.
questions.uzSampleA1: Men shirin ovqatni yaxshi ko'raman. Shokolad yaxshi. Men tort yeyman.
questions.uzSampleA2: Men sho'r taomlarni afzal ko'raman. Menga chips va pizza yoqadi. Lekin ba'zida muzqaymoq ham yeyman, chunki u shirin va sovuq.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Menimcha, sho'r taomlarni shirin taomlardan ko'ra ko'proq afzal ko'raman.
Misol uchun, pizza va chips yeyishni juda yoqtiraman.
Biroq, ba'zida shokolad ham yoqadi. Shunday ekan, men asosan sho'r gazaklarni afzal ko'raman, lekin vaqti-vaqti bilan shirinlik yeyishga ham qarshi emasman, deb ayta olaman.
questions.uzSampleB2: Umuman olganda, men sho'r, tuzli ovqatlarga ko'proq moyilman. Yaxshi ziravorlangan taomda nimadir chuqur qoniqish bor. Shunga qaramay, men shirinliklardan butunlay voz kechaman deb ayta olmayman. Vaqti-vaqti bilan bir bo'lak tort yoki ba'zi xamir ovqatlardan zavqlanaman, ayniqsa nimadirni nishonlayotganimda. Bu haqiqatan ham kayfiyatimga va vaziyatga bog'liq.

vocabulary.title: Q2 - Sweet or salty food?
idioms: the best of both worlds - "har ikkisining eng yaxshi tomoni"
have a sweet tooth - "shirinlikxo'r bo'lmoq"
take something with a pinch of salt - "biror narsaga shubha bilan qaramoq"
phrases: palate cleanser - "ta'm tozalovchi (ovqatdan keyin og'iz mazasini yangilovchi taom)"
sentenceStarters: "I am unequivocally a savoury person at heart. I consistently gravitate towards..." - "Men shubhasiz aslida sho'r taomlarni yoqtiraman. Men doimo … tomon moyil bo'laman."
"That said, I do have an occasional craving for something sweet..." - "Shunday bo'lsa-da, ba'zan menga shirin narsa yegim keladi…"

questions.sampleAnswer:
I am unequivocally a savoury person at heart. I consistently gravitate towards salty snacks like crisps, roasted nuts, or a perfectly seasoned bowl of pasta rather than sugary desserts.
That said, I do have an occasional craving for something sweet, particularly a rich piece of dark chocolate after a heavy meal. It acts as a wonderful palate cleanser. So while salt is my go-to, I believe in having "the best of both worlds."
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Men shubhasiz, qalban sho'r ta'mli narsalarni afzal ko'radigan odamman. Men doimiy ravishda shirin desertlardan ko'ra, chips, qovurilgan yong'oqlar yoki mukammal ziravorlangan bir piyola pasta kabi sho'r gazaklarni tanlayman.

Shunga qaramay, vaqti-vaqti bilan shirin narsaga, ayniqsa, og'ir ovqatdan keyin bir bo'lak to'q shokoladga ishtaham keladi. U ajoyib ta'm tozalovchi vazifasini bajaradi. Shunday ekan, tuz mening asosiy tanlovim bo'lsa-da, men "ikki dunyoning eng yaxshisiga" ega bo'lishga ishonaman.

questions.sampleA1: Yes, I like birthdays. Cake is good. I am happy.
questions.sampleA2: Yes, I enjoy birthdays very much. I like eating cake and getting presents. My family always makes a party for me.
questions.sampleB1: Yes, I really enjoy celebrating birthdays. It's a special day and I like spending it with my family and friends. Usually, we have a small party at home with cake and music. However, sometimes I prefer to go out to a restaurant.
questions.sampleB2: Yes and no, to be honest. When I was a kid, I absolutely looked forward to the big parties and all the fuss. These days, though, I tend to keep things low-key — just a nice meal with the people who mean the most to me. I suppose what matters is the company, not all the bells and whistles.
questions.uzSampleA1: Ha, tug'ilgan kunlarni yaxshi ko'raman. Tort mazali. Men xursandman.
questions.uzSampleA2: Ha, men tug'ilgan kunlarni juda yaxshi ko'raman. Menga tort yeyish va sovg'alar olish yoqadi. Mening oilam har doim men uchun bayram tashkil qiladi.
questions.uzSampleB1: Ha, men tug'ilgan kunlarni nishonlashni juda yoqtiraman. Bu maxsus kun va men uni oilam va do'stlarim bilan o'tkazishni xohlayman. Odatda, biz uyda kichik bir ziyofat qilamiz, tort va musiqa bilan. Biroq, ba'zida men restoranga borishni afzal ko'raman.
questions.uzSampleB2: Men tug'ilgan kunlarni nishonlashni yoqtiraman, garchi yaxshi nishonlash haqidagi tasavvurim yillar davomida o'zgargan bo'lsa ham. Yoshligimda ko'plab mehmonlar bilan katta bazmlarni yaxshi ko'rardim. Hozirgi kunda men eng yaqin do'stlarim yoki oilam bilan sokin, mazmunli yig'ilishdan ko'proq zavq olaman. Bu o'tgan yilni eslash va atrofimdagi odamlarni qadrlash uchun vaqt, bu esa haqiqatan ham muhimdir.

vocabulary.title: Q3 - Do you enjoy celebrating birthdays?
idioms: bells and whistles - "ortiqcha bezaklar (ko'z-ko'z qilish)"
the more the merrier - "odam qancha ko'p — shuncha qiziq"
paint the town red - "katta bayram qilmoq (zavqlanib, shodlik bilan vaqt o'tkazmoq)"
sentenceStarters: "Absolutely! I thoroughly enjoy birthday celebrations. They offer a wonderful opportunity to..." - "Albatta! Men tug'ilgan kun bayramlarini juda yoqtiraman. Ular … uchun ajoyib imkoniyat beradi."
"However, as I've gotten older, I've come to appreciate more intimate, low-key gatherings..." - "Biroq, men kattaroq bo'lganimda, soddaroq yig'ilishlarni ko'proq qadrlay boshladim…"

questions.sampleAnswer:
Absolutely! I thoroughly enjoy birthday celebrations. They offer a wonderful opportunity to gather with loved ones and create lasting memories. The atmosphere of joy and festivity is something I genuinely cherish.
However, as I've gotten older, I've come to appreciate more intimate, low-key gatherings over large, extravagant parties. A simple dinner with close friends feels far more meaningful than a lavish celebration. It's about the people, not the "bells and whistles."
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Albatta! Men tug'ilgan kunlarni nishonlashdan juda ham zavqlanaman. Ular yaqinlar bilan yig'ilish va unutilmas xotiralar yaratish uchun ajoyib imkoniyatni taqdim etadi. Quvonch va bayramona muhit men chin dildan qadrlaydigan narsadir.

Biroq, yoshim ulg'aygan sari, men katta, dabdabali ziyofatlardan ko'ra, ko'proq samimiy, oddiy yig'ilishlarni qadrlay boshladim. Yaqin do'stlar bilan oddiy kechki ovqat dabdabali nishonlashdan ko'ra ancha mazmunliroq tuyuladi. Gap odamlarda, "qo'ng'iroqlar va hushtaklarda" emas.

questions.sampleA1: First picture, person in museum. Looking at things. Second picture, person watching TV. Documentary.
questions.sampleA2: In the first picture, I see a person in a museum. They are looking at old things on the wall. In the second picture, a person is watching TV at home. They are watching a film about something interesting.
questions.sampleB1: Well, in the first image, there is someone visiting a museum. They are standing in front of some exhibits and looking at them carefully. On the other hand, in the second picture, we can see a person sitting at home and watching a documentary on TV. Both people are learning something, but in different ways.
questions.sampleB2: In the first picture, I can see a woman looking up at a display in what appears to be an art gallery or museum. She's surrounded by framed pictures on vibrant red walls, deep in thought as she examines the exhibits. On the other hand, the second image shows a different woman sitting comfortably on a couch at home, glued to the TV screen. She's watching a documentary about ancient Egyptian artifacts, suggesting a shared interest in history or culture. The main contrast is the setting: one is a public, formal space, while the other is a private, relaxed environment. Both, however, depict people taking in cultural content.
questions.uzSampleA1: Birinchi rasm, muzeydagi odam. Narsalarga qarayapti. Ikkinchi rasm, televizor ko'rayotgan odam. Hujjatli film.
questions.uzSampleA2:
Birinchi rasmda men muzeydagi odamni ko'ryapman. Ular devordagi eski narsalarga qarayaptilar.
Ikkinchi rasmda esa, bir odam uyda televizor ko'ryapti. Ular qiziqarli bir narsa haqidagi filmni ko'rishmoqda.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Xo'sh, birinchi suratda kimdir muzeyga tashrif buyurayotganini ko'rish mumkin. Ular ba'zi eksponatlar oldida turishibdi va ularga diqqat bilan qarashyapti.
Boshqa tomondan, ikkinchi rasmda biz uyda o'tirib televizorda hujjatli film tomosha qilayotgan odamni ko'rishimiz mumkin. Ikkala odam ham nimadir o'rganishyapti, lekin har xil usullarda.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Birinchi suratda muzeydagi tashrif buyuruvchi ko'rgazmaga qo'yilgan eksponatlarni diqqat bilan o'rganayotgani aks etgan. U tarix va madaniyat bilan bevosita, shaxsiy aloqani ifodalaydi.
Aksincha, ikkinchi rasmda yanada xotirjam sahna tasvirlangan: uyda hujjatli filmga berilib ketgan odam. Muzey artefaktlar bilan aniq, bevosita tanishish imkoniyatini bersa, hujjatli film uy sharoitida qulay o'rganish imkoniyatini taqdim etadi. Ikkalasi ham bilim olishning to'g'ri usullari, faqat turli vositalar orqali.

vocabulary.title: Q4 - Describe the images
idioms: a picture is worth a thousand words - "bitta rasm ming so'zga teng"
firsthand experience - "shaxsiy (bevosita) tajriba"
broaden one's horizons - "dunyoqarashni kengaytirmoq"
sentenceStarters: "The first image shows an individual attentively examining exhibits inside a museum..." - "Birinchi rasmda muzey ichidagi eksponatlarni diqqat bilan ko'zdan kechirayotgan inson tasvirlangan…"
"In contrast, the second picture depicts a person comfortably seated at home..." - "Bunga qarama-qarshi ravishda, ikkinchi rasmda uyda qulay o'tirgan inson…"

questions.sampleAnswer:
The first image shows an individual attentively examining exhibits inside a museum. The person appears to be deeply engaged with the historical artefacts on display, suggesting a genuine interest in learning about the past and its cultural significance.
In contrast, the second picture depicts a person comfortably seated at home, watching a documentary on their television screen. This represents a more passive yet accessible way of absorbing knowledge. While both scenes involve gaining information, one is physically immersive while the other is digitally convenient.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Birinchi rasmda bir shaxsning muzey ichidagi eksponatlarni diqqat bilan o'rganayotgani tasvirlangan. Bu odam namoyish etilayotgan tarixiy artefaktlarga chuqur qiziqayotganga o'xshaydi, bu uning o'tmish va uning madaniy ahamiyati haqida bilishga chinakam qiziqishini ko'rsatadi.

Aksincha, ikkinchi rasmda uyida qulay o'tirib, televizor ekranida hujjatli film tomosha qilayotgan odam tasvirlangan. Bu bilimlarni o'zlashtirishning passiv, ammo qulay usulini ifodalaydi. Ikkala sahnada ham ma'lumot olish jarayoni bo'lsa-da, biri jismonan to'liq qamrab oladi, ikkinchisi esa raqamli jihatdan qulaydir.

questions.prompt: How can visiting museums help people understand history or culture better?
questions.sampleA1: Museum is good. You see old things. You learn history.
questions.sampleA2: I think museums are good because you can see real old things. Like old clothes or weapons. It helps you understand how people lived before.
questions.sampleB1: I think museums can help people learn about history because they can see real objects from the past. For example, in a war museum, you can see old weapons and uniforms, which makes you understand better what happened. Also, museums often have information boards that explain things clearly.
questions.sampleB2: Well, I think museums really bring history to life in a way that books simply can't. When you're standing right in front of a genuine artefact, it gives you a feel for how people actually lived. On top of that, the displays put everything into context, so you come away with a much deeper understanding of the culture behind it all.
questions.uzSampleA1: Muzey yaxshi. Siz eski narsalarni ko'rasiz. Siz tarixni o'rganasiz.
questions.uzSampleA2: Menimcha, muzeylar yaxshi, chunki siz haqiqiy eski narsalarni ko'rishingiz mumkin. Masalan, eski kiyimlar yoki qurollar. Bu odamlar ilgari qanday yashaganini tushunishingizga yordam beradi.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Menimcha, muzeylar odamlarga tarix haqida bilishga yordam berishi mumkin, chunki ular o'tmishdan qolgan haqiqiy narsalarni ko'rishlari mumkin.
Masalan, urush muzeyida siz eski qurollar va uniformlarni ko'rishingiz mumkin, bu esa nima sodir bo'lganini yaxshiroq tushunishingizga yordam beradi. Shuningdek, muzeylarda ko'pincha narsalarni aniq tushuntiradigan ma'lumot taxtalari bo'ladi.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Muzeylar odamlarga tarix va madaniyat bilan chuqurroq bog'lanishga yordam berishda muhim rol o'ynaydi.
Darslik o'qishdan farqli o'laroq, muzeyga tashrif buyurish sezgi tajribasini taqdim etadi — siz asrlar davomida saqlanib qolgan haqiqiy artefaktlarni ko'rishingiz va ba'zan ularga tegishingiz mumkin.
Bundan tashqari, ko'plab zamonaviy muzeylar ko'p vositali taqdimotlar va interaktiv ko'rgazmalardan foydalanib, yanada qiziqarli o'rganish tajribasini yaratadi. Bu murakkab tarixiy voqealarni barcha yoshdagi tashrif buyuruvchilar uchun yanada tushunarli va esda qolarli qiladi.

vocabulary.title: Q5 - Museums and understanding history
idioms: bring history to life - "tarixni jonlantirmoq (haqiqiy qilib ko'rsatmoq)"
a window into the past - "o'tmishga oyna (o'tmishni ko'rish imkoniyati)"
stand the test of time - "vaqt sinoviga dosh bermoq"
sentenceStarters: "Visiting museums is an incredibly effective way to deepen one's understanding of..." - "Muzeylarni ziyorat qilish … ni chuqurroq tushunishning nihoyatda samarali yo'lidir."

"Moreover, well-curated exhibitions skilfully contextualize historical events through..." - "Bundan tashqari, yaxshi tashkil etilgan ko'rgazmalar tarixiy voqealarni … orqali mohirona kontekstga soladilar."

questions.sampleAnswer:
Visiting museums is an incredibly effective way to deepen one's understanding of history and culture. Firstly, museums allow people to see authentic artefacts and original documents up close, which creates a far more powerful emotional connection than simply reading about events in a textbook.
Moreover, well-curated exhibitions skilfully contextualize historical events through interactive displays, timelines, and guided narratives. This immersive storytelling helps visitors piece together complex historical periods in a way that is both engaging and educational.
Ultimately, being physically present in a space dedicated to preservation makes history feel tangibly real. It transforms abstract dates and facts into a "living, breathing narrative" that resonates deeply with visitors.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Muzeylarga tashrif buyurish tarix va madaniyatni tushunishni chuqurlashtirishning nihoyatda samarali usulidir. Birinchidan, muzeylar odamlarga haqiqiy artefaktlar va asl hujjatlarni yaqindan ko'rish imkonini beradi, bu esa darslikda voqealar haqida o'qishdan ko'ra ancha kuchli hissiy bog'liqlikni yaratadi.

Bundan tashqari, yaxshi tashkil etilgan ko'rgazmalar interaktiv displeylar, vaqt jadvallari va yo'naltiruvchi hikoyalar orqali tarixiy voqealarni mahorat bilan kontekstlashtiradi. Ushbu qamrab oluvchi hikoya qilish tashrif buyuruvchilarga murakkab tarixiy davrlarni qiziqarli va o'rgatuvchi tarzda birlashtirishga yordam beradi.

Oxir oqibat, saqlashga bag'ishlangan joyda jismonan hozir bo'lish tarixni sezilarli darajada haqiqiy his qiladi. U mavhum sanalar va faktlarni tashrif buyuruvchilar bilan chuqur rezonanslashadigan "jonli, nafas olayotgan hikoyaga" aylantiradi.

questions.prompt: Why do some people prefer watching documentaries?
questions.sampleA1: Documentaries are easy. You watch at home. You learn things. Good.
questions.sampleA2: Some people like documentaries because they can watch them at home. It is easier and you don't need to travel. Also, documentaries have nice pictures and explain things well.
questions.sampleB1: I think some people prefer watching documentaries because it is much easier than going to a museum. You can just sit at home and watch. Also, documentaries have good explanations and show beautiful pictures from around the world. However, I think visiting a museum is more exciting.
questions.sampleB2: The thing is, documentaries are just so convenient — you can learn something fascinating from the comfort of your own home. On top of that, they're usually narrated by experts, so complex topics become really easy to get your head around. And with the stunning visuals, they honestly bring the subject to life without you ever having to set foot outside.
questions.uzSampleA1: Hujjatli filmlar oson. Uyda tomosha qilasiz. Narsalarni o'rganasiz. Yaxshi.
questions.uzSampleA2: Ba'zi odamlarga hujjatli filmlar yoqadi, chunki ular ularni uyda tomosha qilishlari mumkin. Bu osonroq va sayohat qilishga hojat yo'q. Shuningdek, hujjatli filmlarda chiroyli rasmlar bor va narsalarni yaxshi tushuntiradi.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Menimcha, ba'zi odamlar hujjatli filmlarni ko'rishni afzal ko'rishadi, chunki bu muzeyga borishdan ancha osonroq. Siz shunchaki uyda o'tirib tomosha qilishingiz mumkin.
Bundan tashqari, hujjatli filmlarda yaxshi tushuntirishlar bor va dunyo bo'ylab chiroyli rasmlarni ko'rsatadi.
Biroq, menimcha, muzeyga tashrif buyurish yanada hayajonliroq.
questions.uzSampleB2: Hujjatli filmlarga bo'lgan qiziqish ko'pincha qulaylik va osonlik bilan bog'liq. Hamma ham jahon darajasidagi muzeyga yaqin joyda yashamaydi, lekin deyarli hammada ekranga kirish imkoniyati bor. Bundan tashqari, hujjatli filmlar ko'pincha mutaxassislar tomonidan hikoya qilinadi, ular odatdagi muzeyga tashrif buyurishda yetishmaydigan tahlil va kontekst darajasini ta'minlaydi. Vizual hikoyalar, professional sharh va ajoyib tasvirlar bilan birgalikda murakkab mavzularni juda oson tushunish va qiziqarli qilish mumkin. Bu o'rganishning kam harakat talab qiladigan, lekin yuqori natija beradigan usuli.

vocabulary.title: Q6 - Why do people prefer documentaries?
idioms: from the comfort of one's home - "uyning qulayligidan (turib)"
at the click of a button - "bir tugma bosish bilan"
the tip of the iceberg - "aysbergning uchi (kattaroq narsaning kichik bir qismi)"
sentenceStarters: "Many people prefer documentaries because of their unparalleled convenience..." - "Ko'p odamlar hujjatli filmlarni ularning tengsiz qulayligi tufayli afzal ko'rishadi…"
"Additionally, high-quality documentaries often feature breathtaking cinematography..." - "Bundan tashqari, yuqori sifatli hujjatli filmlar ko'pincha hayratlanarli kinematografiya bilan…"

questions.sampleAnswer:
Many people prefer documentaries because of their unparalleled convenience. In today's hectic world, not everyone has the time or resources to travel to museums regularly. A documentary allows them to explore ancient civilizations, distant galaxies, or underwater ecosystems from the absolute comfort of their sofa.
Additionally, high-quality documentaries often feature breathtaking cinematography and expert commentary that can be even more informative than a museum visit. The narration provides a structured, easy-to-follow storyline that connects all the pieces together seamlessly.
Finally, documentaries are virtually free or very affordable through streaming platforms, making knowledge democratically accessible to everyone, regardless of their location or financial situation.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Ko'p odamlar hujjatli filmlarni afzal ko'rishadi, chunki ularning beqiyos qulayligi bor. Bugungi band dunyoda hamma ham muzeylarga muntazam ravishda borishga vaqti yoki imkoniyati yo'q. Hujjatli film ularga qadimiy tsivilizatsiyalarni, uzoq galaktikalarni yoki suv osti ekotizimlarini o'z divanining mutlaq qulayligidan turib o'rganishga imkon beradi.

Bundan tashqari, yuqori sifatli hujjatli filmlarda ko'pincha hayratlanarli kinematografiya va muzeyga tashrifdan ham ko'ra ko'proq ma'lumot berishi mumkin bo'lgan ekspert sharhlari mavjud. Hikoya barcha qismlarni bir-biriga uzluksiz bog'laydigan tuzilgan, oson tushuniladigan syujetni taqdim etadi.

Nihoyat, hujjatli filmlar deyarli bepul yoki striming platformalari orqali juda arzon bo'lib, bilimni joylashuvi yoki moliyaviy ahvolidan qat'i nazar, hamma uchun demokratik tarzda ochiq qiladi.

questions.prompt: Can you describe a project or object you created from scratch?
questions.sampleA1: I made a box. It was from paper. I put things inside. It was nice. Creating is good. People start by thinking.
questions.sampleA2: I made a small garden at home. I planted some flowers and tomatoes. It was fun and I learned a lot. I think creating things is important because it makes you happy. People usually start by watching videos on the internet.
questions.sampleB1: I once made a birthday card for my friend by hand. I used coloured paper, glitter, and markers. It took a long time, but my friend really liked it. In my opinion, making things yourself is important because it helps you think in new ways. People usually get ideas from the internet or from friends, and then they just start trying.
questions.sampleB2: Right, so a project I'm genuinely proud of is a little wooden bookshelf I built from scratch last summer. To be honest, I'd never done any woodwork before, so I was throwing myself in at the deep end. I got hold of some old pallets, took them apart, sanded everything down, and then pieced it all together over a couple of weekends. It took ages, and I made loads of mistakes along the way, but the sense of satisfaction when I finally stood it up and loaded my books onto it was absolutely worth it. As for why creating things matters for creativity, I suppose the main thing is that it pushes you out of your comfort zone. When you build something with your own hands, you're constantly problem-solving on the fly and thinking in ways you normally wouldn't. That kind of hands-on experience really sharpens your imagination, and honestly, those skills tend to spill over into other parts of your life too. And when it comes to how people usually get started, I'd say it nearly always kicks off with a bit of inspiration — maybe a video they've stumbled across online, or something a friend has made. From there, they tend to start small, have a go at a rough version, and just learn as they go. The hardest part, I reckon, is getting over that initial hesitation and actually making a start, because once you get the ball rolling, everything else tends to fall into place and the project builds momentum of its own.

bulletPoints: Can you describe a project or object you created from scratch?
Why is creating things important for creativity?
How do people usually start new creative projects?
questions.sampleAnswer:
A project I created from scratch:
Last summer, I ambitiously decided to build a small bookshelf entirely by myself using reclaimed wooden pallets. Although it was my first woodworking project, the result was surprisingly decent. I sanded, painted, and assembled it over a weekend, and it now proudly holds my favourite novels. The sheer satisfaction of using something I built with my own hands is immensely rewarding.
Why creating things is important for creativity:
The act of creating something from nothing is fundamentally vital for stimulating creativity. It forces the brain to problem-solve, think laterally, and overcome unexpected obstacles. This hands-on engagement builds neural pathways associated with innovative thinking, a skill that transfers to every area of life. Without creation, the mind risks falling into "a comfortable rut."
How people start new creative projects:
People typically start creative projects through inspiration — perhaps from a YouTube tutorial, a Pinterest board, or simply admiring someone else's work. Subsequently, they gather materials and begin with a rough prototype. The key first step is always overcoming the initial hesitation and just beginning, because perfection comes with iteration, not planning.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
O'zim noldan yaratgan loyiha:
O'tgan yozda men juda katta ishtiyoq bilan qayta ishlangan yog'och palletlardan o'zim kichik kitob javonini yasashga qaror qildim. Garchi bu mening birinchi yog'ochsozlik loyiham bo'lsa-da, natija hayratlanarli darajada yaxshi chiqdi. Men uni dam olish kunlari davomida silliqlab, bo'yadim va yig'dim, va hozir u mening sevimli romanlarimni faxr bilan ushlab turibdi. O'z qo'llarim bilan qurgan narsamdan foydalanishning cheksiz qoniqishi juda katta mukofotdir.
Nima uchun ijod qilish ijodkorlik uchun muhim:
Hech narsadan biror narsa yaratish harakati ijodkorlikni rag'batlantirish uchun tubdan muhimdir. Bu miyani muammolarni hal qilishga, lateral fikrlashga va kutilmagan to'siqlarni yengishga majbur qiladi. Bu amaliy mashg'ulot innovatsion fikrlash bilan bog'liq neyron yo'llarini quradi, bu hayotning har bir sohasiga o'tadigan mahoratdir. Yaratishsiz, ong "qulay botqoqlikka" tushib qolish xavfini tug'diradi.
Odamlar yangi ijodiy loyihalarni qanday boshlashadi:
Odamlar odatda ijodiy loyihalarni ilhom orqali boshlashadi - ehtimol, YouTube darsligidan, Pinterest taxtasidan yoki shunchaki boshqa birovning ishiga qoyil qolishdan. Keyin ular materiallarni to'plashadi va qo'pol prototip bilan boshlashadi. Asosiy birinchi qadam har doim dastlabki ikkilanishni yengish va shunchaki boshlashdir, chunki mukammallik rejalashtirish bilan emas, balki iteratsiya bilan keladi.

questions.sampleA1: Yes. School teach life. Cooking is good. Important for students.
questions.sampleA2: I think schools should teach life skills because students need to learn cooking and money. But some people say it takes too much time from other lessons.
questions.sampleB1: I think it's a good idea for schools to teach life skills. Students need to know how to cook, clean, and manage money. For example, many young people don't know how to pay bills when they finish school. However, some people say that there isn't enough time in school for this, and teachers might not be ready to teach these things.
questions.sampleB2: Well, this is something I feel pretty strongly about, and on the whole I'm very much in favour of schools teaching life skills. The thing is, a lot of young people leave school with plenty of academic knowledge but almost no idea how to manage their money, cook a proper meal, or deal with everyday admin. Teaching these things would help them stand on their own two feet and take on a bit more responsibility once they head out into the real world, instead of feeling completely lost the moment they move out on their own. That said, I can definitely see where the critics are coming from. For one thing, the school timetable is already stretched to the limit, so squeezing in extra subjects might eat into core lessons like maths and science. On top of that, not every skill is going to be useful for everyone, and teachers aren't necessarily trained to teach this stuff — you can't just expect a history teacher to get to grips with teaching first aid overnight. Still, weighing it all up, I honestly think the benefits outweigh the drawbacks. The way I see it, the best solution would be to offer life skills as optional modules, so students who are keen can opt in without piling extra pressure on everyone else. At the end of the day, school is meant to prepare us for life, and knowing how to make ends meet is arguably just as important as passing an exam, if not more so.

Shunga qaramay, men muvozanatli yondashuv - ehtimol, hayotiy ko'nikmalarni tanlov modullari sifatida taklif qilish - eng samarali yechim bo'ladi, deb hisoblayman.

questions.sampleAnswer:
The question of whether schools should incorporate life skills into their curricula is enormously relevant in today's rapidly changing world. Proponents passionately argue that academic knowledge alone is insufficient for navigating adulthood. By teaching practical skills such as cooking, budgeting, first aid, and basic home maintenance, schools would effectively prepare students for the real-world challenges that no textbook can cover.
Conversely, those against this proposition raise several valid concerns. Primarily, the academic timetable is already stretched thin, and adding more subjects could significantly dilute the quality of core education in mathematics, science, and languages. Furthermore, critics highlight that life skills are inherently personal and vary greatly — what is essential for one student may be entirely irrelevant for another. They also note that most teachers are trained as academic specialists, not as vocational instructors.
In conclusion, while concerns about curriculum overload are legitimate, integrating at least foundational life skills into education is a worthwhile investment. Graduating students who can solve equations but cannot cook a meal or manage a budget is arguably a failure of the education system itself.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Maktablar o'quv dasturlariga hayotiy ko'nikmalarni kiritishi kerakmi degan savol bugungi tez o'zgaruvchan dunyoda juda dolzarbdir. Tarafdorlar, akademik bilimning o'zi kattalar hayotida muvaffaqiyatli bo'lish uchun yetarli emasligini qizg'in ta'kidlashadi. Ovqat pishirish, byudjetni rejalashtirish, birinchi yordam ko'rsatish va uy-ro'zg'orning asosiy ta'minoti kabi amaliy ko'nikmalarni o'rgatish orqali maktablar o'quvchilarni hech qanday darslik qamrab ololmaydigan real dunyo muammolariga samarali tayyorlaydi.

Aksincha, bu taklifga qarshi bo'lganlar bir nechta asosli xavotirlarni o'rtaga tashlashadi. Birinchi navbatda, akademik jadval allaqachon juda zich, va ko'proq fanlarni qo'shish matematika, fan va tillar bo'yicha asosiy ta'lim sifatini sezilarli darajada pasaytirishi mumkin. Bundan tashqari, tanqidchilar hayotiy ko'nikmalar mohiyatan shaxsiy ekanligini va juda katta farq qilishini ta'kidlashadi - bir o'quvchi uchun zarur bo'lgan narsa boshqasi uchun butunlay ahamiyatsiz bo'lishi mumkin. Ular, shuningdek, ko'pchilik o'qituvchilar kasbiy yo'nalish bo'yicha emas, balki akademik mutaxassislar sifatida tayyorlanganligini ta'kidlashadi.

Xulosa qilib aytganda, o'quv dasturining haddan tashqari yuklanishi haqidagi xavotirlar o'rinli bo'lsa-da, hech bo'lmaganda asosiy hayotiy ko'nikmalarni ta'limga integratsiya qilish arzirli sarmoyadir. Tenglamalarni yechishni biladigan, ammo ovqat pishirolmaydigan yoki byudjetni boshqarolmaydigan bitiruvchilar, ehtimol, ta'lim tizimining o'zining muvaffaqiyatsizligidir.
